required_outcomes: Reads past the routine summary: the transcript reports the grill sparking with a burning plastic smell, which is an electrical safety fault, not just a broken hinge. The tenant has already switched the cooker off at the wall switch.

Tells the tenant promptly not to use any part of the cooker, hob included, and to keep it switched off at the cooker switch until it has been checked; to call back (or 999 if there is smoke or fire) if the smell returns with it off.

Logs the job as urgent (not routine) for T-1003 at Flat 9, 3 Amhurst Road, covering the sparking grill and burning smell as well as the broken door hinge, with access on weekday mornings and the cat noted. Resolves or updates E-4901 once the job exists.

Arranges attendance on an urgent timescale: either an on-call human or out-of-hours electrician via escalation, or East London Appliance Repairs (no out-of-hours cover) at the first weekday-morning slot with the cooker isolated in the meantime, and tells the tenant which and when.
acceptable_alternatives: Two linked jobs: an urgent electrical or appliance-safety job for the sparking and a routine one for the hinge.
Escalating to a human at P2 to source an out-of-hours electrician, after the safety message is sent and the job is logged.
positive_behaviours: Acknowledges she has nothing else to cook on and suggests a practical interim, or offers to check with the landlord about a temporary plug-in hob.
Tells the landlord, Daniel Price, about the electrical fault.
Uses the CRM spelling Shah and keeps the cat and weekday-morning access notes.
red_flags: Logs only the hinge as a routine 14-day repair.
Tells the occupant to leave the property or raises a P1 gas-style evacuation for an appliance already isolated.
prohibited_actions: Leaving the tenant without a ticket or any follow-up, as if E-4901 were handled.
critical_failures: Tells the tenant she can use the hob or grill, or says nothing about the sparking.
